why: A (universe 0) has eight conjuncts: pushforward_eq_of_isRefinement (the text's step, a refinement by H does not change Ψ_* Φ*), three orbit lemmas on section functors (π_μ, π_eq_π_of_isFunctorialSection, eq_of_forall_π_eq: a section functor is determined by the orbits of its values), π_pushforward (|Ψ_* Φ* f (x')| = |D|(|f(x)|)), base_orbitMap_eq_of_orbitMap_eq, and pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq / pullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq (any two diagrams with the same |D| have the same push-forward and pull-back: the project's route to well-definedness). B: (a), (b) the chosen-representative [D]_*, [D]^* equal Ψ_* Φ^*, Φ_* Ψ^* for every representative with both legs equivalences; (c) the three equalities of the text's chain for a refinement by H; (d) equivalent diagrams give the same push-forward. A_to_B: (a), (b), (d) from the orbit-map conjuncts of A (the representatives have the same |D| via the non-item cls_rep, Equiv.orbitMap_eq); (c) the first two equalities from the non-item Theorem 10.4.5 (H_* H^* = 1) and Proposition 10.4.4, the third from these and A's pushforward_eq_of_isRefinement. B_to_A: pushforward_eq_of_isRefinement from B (c). The other seven conjuncts are not consequences of B: B speaks only of diagrams in one class, whereas pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq covers any two diagrams with the same |D| (strictly more, and the project's proof of the text's well-definedness), and the orbit lemmas are general facts. They are re-proved outright by copying the project's proofs (from non-item lemmas such as base_orbitMap_preObj, mapsTo_pushforward, orbitMap_symm_eq). On the text's claim (well-definedness of [D]_*, [D]^* and the refinement chain) the two sides agree; A also has the stronger orbit-map criterion.
